title: Adiabatic controlled-$Z$ gate for neutral atoms with Förster-enhanced Rydberg dressing
abstract: We study an adiabatic controlled-$Z$ (CZ) gate for neutral atoms in which dipole-dipole coupling between nearly degenerate Rydberg pair states enhances the interaction between dressed ground states. This coupling produces an avoided crossing in the two-atom dressed-state spectrum. Approaching the crossing enhances the dressed interaction, but also reduces the dressed-state gap and increases the Rydberg admixture. We identify a Förster-enhanced operating range in which the required conditional phase is accumulated with adiabatic return and small transient Rydberg population. We then analyze the finite-time dynamics of the two-qubit computational states under a smooth pulse. Reducing the dressing strength weakens the dressed interaction, so maintaining the target phase at the same pulse duration requires operation closer to the avoided crossing, where the Rydberg admixture increases. This dependence is then used to select the shortest gate at a fixed peak Rabi frequency in the Förster-enhanced operating range that accumulates the CZ phase with high Bell-state fidelity while keeping the Rydberg population small. Changing the Förster defect shifts the avoided crossing, while the gate parameters change only weakly. For a specific rubidium Förster channel, the selected gate corresponds to experimentally relevant laser coupling, pulse duration, and interatomic separation. We also estimate errors from the finite Rydberg lifetime and from weak excitation of a neighboring spectator atom. For the parameters considered, the spectator-induced error remains below the finite-lifetime contribution.
summary: This paper details the theoretical design of an adiabatic controlled-Z gate for neutral atoms by exploiting Förster-enhanced dipole-dipole coupling in Rydberg dressed states. The authors determine an optimal operating regime that maximizes the gate interaction while keeping the Rydberg excitation probability low. They rigorously analyze gate fidelity by accounting for both finite Rydberg lifetime and parasitic interactions from spectator atoms.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of implementing an adiabatic controlled-Z (CZ) gate for neutral atoms by leveraging Förster-enhanced dipole-dipole coupling between Rydberg pair states.
main_result: They identify an optimal operating range where the required conditional phase is accumulated with high fidelity while minimizing transient Rydberg population, and they quantify the error contributions from finite lifetime and spectator atoms.
method: The analysis uses time-dependent quantum simulation, tracking the evolution of dressed states under a smooth pulse, and calculating the accumulated conditional phase $\phi_{CZ}(T)$.
model_or_system: The system involves neutral atoms trapped in optical tweezers, using hyperfine ground states as qubits, with entanglement mediated by excitation to Rydberg states. The Hamiltonian models single-atom and two-atom interactions, incorporating the Förster defect $\delta_p$.
key_observables: Conditional phase ($\phi_{CZ}$), Bell-state fidelity ($F_{Bell}$), maximum Rydberg population ($P_{max}^{Ryd}$), and spectator-induced phase shift ($\Delta F_{talk}$).
important_parameters: Dipole-dipole coupling strength ($B$), Rabi frequency ($\Omega$), Förster defect ($\delta_p$), and pulse duration ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes adiabatic evolution is possible in the identified operating range, and error sources are quantified separately (lifetime vs. spectator interaction).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy level structure and Rydberg dressing (Fig. 1), the dependence of the effective interaction $\kappa$ on coupling strength $B$ (Fig. 2, 3), and the time-dependent dynamics showing population evolution and phase accumulation (Fig. 9, 10).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and the role of Förster enhancement in generating the necessary interaction. It then analyzes the time-dependent dynamics to select optimal pulse parameters, followed by a detailed analysis of error sources, including spectator atom interactions.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, quantitative roadmap for building quantum gates using highly controllable, long-range interactions inherent to Rydberg atoms, which is a cornerstone of modern quantum simulation and computing.
